name: Responsibility
overview: Scripture reveals that responsibility involves owning one's actions rather than shifting blame, as seen when Adam and Eve each deflect their guilt (Genesis 3:12-13). This theme continues with figures like Sarah, who places blame on Abram for her circumstances (Genesis 16:5), and Esau, who laments the loss of his birthright and blessing (Genesis 27:36). Aaron's attempt to excuse the people's mischief (Exodus 32:22) contrasts with the wisdom of confessing and forsaking sins to receive mercy (Proverbs 28:13), emphasizing personal accountability as essential before God.
